title: The Village Voted for Nobody
layout: Six fullscreen vertical slides. Each slide expands one comic beat into a single dominant scene with large post lettering and central safe areas.

units.title: The hook
units.purpose: Make the result legible before introducing village procedure.
units.scene: The bright holders room with polished mahogany and the new Town Hall visible through the tall window in daylight.
units.action: Barkeep freezes mid-polish, leans toward the reader with a knowing look, and gestures toward Town Hall.
units.composition: Fullscreen 9:16 poster composition, Barkeep fills the lower center, Town Hall remains readable above the shoulder, generous empty headline area at the top and small caption area at the bottom
continuity: Barkeep uses the approved base-cat sheet with no added wardrobe.
The polishing cloth appears exactly once.
Use the same cream, charcoal, teal, and brass print palette as every later slide.

units.title: The question
units.purpose: Explain what the village actually voted on.
units.scene: Inside the bright Town Hall chamber with cream stone, teal trim, brass ballot hardware, civic podium, resident silhouettes, and one oversized empty mayor's chair.
units.action: Clerk opens the dark teal ballot ledger and presents one blank ballot strip toward the empty mayor's chair.
units.composition: Fullscreen 9:16 scene with Clerk large in the center, empty chair looming behind, open headline area above and civic note area below

postText.headline: SHALL THE VILLAGE ELECT A MAYOR?
captions: ELECTED WEEKLY. RECALLABLE. VOICE AND AGENDA. NO COMMAND POWER.

continuity: The mayor's chair remains completely empty.
Clerk uses the approved cream civic vest and no other costume.
The ballot ledger and one blank ballot strip appear exactly once.

units.title: The Yes vote
units.purpose: Give Barkeep's practical argument its own full scene.
units.scene: Back in the same holders room, with Town Hall still visible through the window and one fixed Yes placard built into the counter.
units.action: Barkeep plants one gloved finger on the fixed Yes placard while gripping the folded polishing cloth in the other hand.
units.composition: Fullscreen 9:16 low-angle comic pose, Barkeep dominates the frame, open speech area above the pointing arm, keep hands fully visible

dialogue.speaker: barkeep
dialogue.text: SOMEONE'S GOTTA TAKE THE HEAT WHEN THE PLUMBING SHITS THE BED.

continuity: Match the holders-room geometry and daylight from slide one.
Barkeep has exactly two arms and two gloved hands.

units.title: The No vote
units.purpose: Give Critic's process argument its own full scene.
units.scene: Inside the same Town Hall chamber, with the empty mayor's chair behind Critic and resident silhouettes watching.
units.action: Critic taps the black review slate with the cream pencil, raises one skeptical eyebrow, and looks past the reader toward the empty chair.
units.composition: Fullscreen 9:16 medium close-up with Critic large and the empty chair visible over one shoulder, one large open speech area above

dialogue.speaker: critic
dialogue.text: WE HAVE A CLERK AND AN OFFICER. WE DO NOT NEED A MASCOT.

continuity: Match the Town Hall geometry, crowd palette, and daylight from slide two.
Critic has only the approved heavier eyebrows and no added costume.
The black review slate and cream pencil appear exactly once.

units.title: The result
units.purpose: Deliver the exact certified count as the visual climax.
units.scene: The same Town Hall chamber and podium, crowded with residents while the empty mayor's chair remains visible in the background.
units.action: Teller snaps the final bead into place on the compact brass abacus and presents one blank receipt toward the reader.
units.composition: Fullscreen 9:16 energetic centered composition, Teller and abacus in the lower half, large empty result board in the upper half

dialogue.speaker: teller
dialogue.text: THE VILLAGE REMAINS WITHOUT A MAYOR.

continuity: Match the Town Hall geometry, crowd palette, and daylight from slides two and four.
Teller uses the approved teal accountant visor.
The compact brass abacus and one blank receipt appear exactly once.

units.title: The payoff
units.purpose: End on the empty office and Gaspard's exact joke.
units.scene: The same Town Hall chamber in calm morning light, the untouched empty mayor's chair centered, and the working town visible through the windows.
units.action: Gaspard stands beside the empty chair, holds the round mirror low, closes the gallery ledger, and looks directly at the reader without smiling.
units.composition: Fullscreen 9:16 quiet closing poster, empty chair is the primary focal point and Gaspard stands at the lower edge, large caption area above and final speech area below

postText.headline: THE VILLAGE VOTED FOR A VOID IN THE MAYOR'S OFFICE.

dialogue.speaker: gaspard
dialogue.text: FINALLY, A POLITICIAN WHO DOESN'T LIE ABOUT HIS INTENTIONS. BOF.

continuity: Match the Town Hall geometry and palette from all prior civic slides.
Gaspard uses the approved black beret and cream stained smock.
No candidate, portrait, crown, sash, or mayor character appears.
